992	void qr_coop_launch(int64_t A_ptr, int64_t Acm_ptr, int64_t H_ptr, int64_t tau_ptr,
993	                    int64_t Tg_ptr, int64_t gbar_ptr, int n, int NB, int gridcap) {
994	    const float* A = reinterpret_cast<const float*>(A_ptr);
995	    float* Acm = reinterpret_cast<float*>(Acm_ptr);
996	    float* H = reinterpret_cast<float*>(H_ptr);
997	    float* tau = reinterpret_cast<float*>(tau_ptr);
998	    float* Tg = reinterpret_cast<float*>(Tg_ptr);
999	    unsigned int* g_bar = reinterpret_cast<unsigned int*>(gbar_ptr);
1000	    const int TPB = 256;
1001	    const int CT = 32;       // trailing column-tile width per CTA
1002	    const int RB = 64;       // V row-strip height staged through smem
1003	    switch (NB) {
1004	        case 8:  coop_dispatch<TPB, 8,  CT, RB>(A, Acm, H, tau, Tg, g_bar, n, gridcap); break;
1005	        case 16: coop_dispatch<TPB, 16, CT, RB>(A, Acm, H, tau, Tg, g_bar, n, gridcap); break;
1006	        case 24: coop_dispatch<TPB, 24, CT, RB>(A, Acm, H, tau, Tg, g_bar, n, gridcap); break;
1007	        case 32: coop_dispatch<TPB, 32, CT, RB>(A, Acm, H, tau, Tg, g_bar, n, gridcap); break;
1008	        default: coop_dispatch<TPB, 16, CT, RB>(A, Acm, H, tau, Tg, g_bar, n, gridcap); break;
1009	    }
1010	}

1012	// ===========================================================================
1013	// BATCHED TWO-KERNEL blocked QR for large n (n>1024), small batch B.
1014	//   The grid-barrier megakernel above is occupancy-limited to 12.5% because its
1015	//   per-block smem = n*NB (panel sub-panel) forces 1 block/SM EVEN for the
1016	//   trailing update (the dominant work). This version splits panel factor and
1017	//   trailing update into SEPARATE kernel launches (the launch boundary is the
1018	//   barrier -- NO cross-CTA atomics needed, capturable). The trailing kernel
1019	//   uses a tiny smem footprint -> high occupancy + a large grid; the panel
1020	//   kernel runs B blocks (one per matrix), so its big smem only costs B SMs.
1021	//   All B matrices are factored CONCURRENTLY (panel kernel = B blocks; trailing
1022	//   kernel grid-strides over (matrix, column-tile) work items).
1023	// Acm: column-major B*n*n. Tg: B*NBMAX*NBMAX compact-WY T. tau: B*n.
1024	// ===========================================================================
1025	
1026	// transpose row-major A (B,n,n) -> column-major Acm (per matrix Acm[b][c*n+r]).
1027	__global__ void qr_transpose_in(const float* __restrict__ A, float* __restrict__ Acm,
1028	                                int B, int n) {
1029	    const size_t total = (size_t)B * n * n;
1030	    for (size_t idx = (size_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; idx < total;
1031	         idx += (size_t)gridDim.x * blockDim.x) {
1032	        int b = idx / ((size_t)n * n);
1033	        size_t rem = idx - (size_t)b * n * n;
1034	        int r = rem / n, c = rem % n;
1035	        Acm[(size_t)b * n * n + (size_t)c * n + r] = A[(size_t)b * n * n + (size_t)r * n + c];
1036	    }
1037	}
1038	__global__ void qr_transpose_out(const float* __restrict__ Acm, float* __restrict__ H,
1039	                                 int B, int n) {
1040	    const size_t total = (size_t)B * n * n;
1041	    for (size_t idx = (size_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; idx < total;
1042	         idx += (size_t)gridDim.x * blockDim.x) {
1043	        int b = idx / ((size_t)n * n);
1044	        size_t rem = idx - (size_t)b * n * n;
1045	        int r = rem / n, c = rem % n;
1046	        H[(size_t)b * n * n + (size_t)r * n + c] = Acm[(size_t)b * n * n + (size_t)c * n + r];
1047	    }
1048	}

1050	// PANEL FACTOR kernel: grid = B (block b factors matrix b's panel [p,p+nb)).
1051	// Active sub-panel rows[p,n) x nb loaded into dynamic smem (ldp*nb floats,
1052	// sized by the host for this p), factored on-chip; reflectors+R written back to
1053	// Acm[b]; compact-WY T built into Tg[b]. Identical math to coop_panel_factor.
1054	template <int TPB, int NBMAX>
1055	__global__ void qr_panel_kernel(float* __restrict__ Acm_all, float* __restrict__ Tg_all,
1056	                                float* __restrict__ tau_all, int B, int n, int p, int nb) {
1057	    extern __shared__ float Ps[];          // ldp * nb (col-major Ps[rr + j*ldp])
1058	    const int b = blockIdx.x;
1059	    if (b >= B) return;
1060	    float* Acm = Acm_all + (size_t)b * n * n;
1061	    float* Tg  = Tg_all + (size_t)b * NBMAX * NBMAX;
1062	    float* taub = tau_all + (size_t)b * n;
1063	
1064	    const int NWARP = TPB / 32;
1065	    const int REDSZ = (NBMAX * NWARP > TPB) ? NBMAX * NWARP : TPB;
1066	    __shared__ float red[REDSZ];
1067	    __shared__ float sval[4];
1068	    __shared__ float zsh[NBMAX];
1069	    __shared__ float taus[NBMAX];
1070	    const int tid = threadIdx.x;
1071	    const int lane = tid & 31, warp = tid >> 5;
1072	    const int ldp = n - p;
1073	
1074	    for (int idx = tid; idx < ldp * nb; idx += TPB) {
1075	        int j = idx / ldp, rr = idx % ldp;
1076	        Ps[rr + j * ldp] = Acm[(size_t)(p + j) * n + (p + rr)];
1077	    }
1078	    __syncthreads();
1079	
1080	    for (int j = 0; j < nb; ++j) {
1081	        float* pj = Ps + (size_t)j * ldp;
1082	        int rj = j;
1083	        float partial = 0.f;
1084	        for (int rr = rj + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) { float x = pj[rr]; partial += x * x; }
1085	        red[tid] = partial; __syncthreads();
1086	        for (int s = TPB / 2; s > 0; s >>= 1) { if (tid < s) red[tid] += red[tid + s]; __syncthreads(); }
1087	        if (tid == 0) {
1088	            float xnorm = sqrtf(red[0]);
1089	            float alpha = pj[rj];
1090	            float beta = (alpha >= 0.f) ? -xnorm : xnorm;
1091	            float tval, invden;
1092	            if (xnorm > 0.f && (alpha - beta) != 0.f) {
1093	                tval = (beta - alpha) / beta; invden = 1.f / (alpha - beta);
1094	            } else { tval = 0.f; invden = 0.f; beta = alpha; }
1095	            sval[0] = beta; sval[1] = tval; sval[2] = invden;
1096	        }
1097	        __syncthreads();
1098	        float beta = sval[0], tval = sval[1], invden = sval[2];
1099	        for (int rr = rj + 1 + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) pj[rr] *= invden;
1100	        __syncthreads();
1101	        if (tid == 0) { pj[rj] = 1.f; taus[j] = tval; }
1102	        __syncthreads();
1103	        int ntrail = nb - (j + 1);
1104	        if (ntrail > 0) {
1105	            float pw[NBMAX];
1106	            #pragma unroll
1107	            for (int t = 0; t < NBMAX; ++t) pw[t] = 0.f;
1108	            for (int rr = rj + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) {
1109	                float vr = pj[rr];
1110	                for (int t = 0; t < ntrail; ++t)
1111	                    pw[t] += vr * Ps[(size_t)(j + 1 + t) * ldp + rr];
1112	            }
1113	            for (int t = 0; t < ntrail; ++t) {
1114	                float v = pw[t];
1115	                #pragma unroll
1116	                for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) v += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, v, o);
1117	                if (lane == 0) red[t * NWARP + warp] = v;
1118	            }
1119	            __syncthreads();
1120	            if (tid < ntrail) {
1121	                float w = 0.f;
1122	                for (int wi = 0; wi < NWARP; ++wi) w += red[tid * NWARP + wi];
1123	                zsh[tid] = tval * w;
1124	            }
1125	            __syncthreads();
1126	            for (int t = 0; t < ntrail; ++t) {
1127	                float tw = zsh[t];
1128	                float* pjj = Ps + (size_t)(j + 1 + t) * ldp;
1129	                for (int rr = rj + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) pjj[rr] -= tw * pj[rr];
1130	            }
1131	            __syncthreads();
1132	        }
1133	        if (tid == 0) pj[rj] = beta;
1134	        __syncthreads();
1135	    }
1136	    for (int i = tid; i < nb; i += TPB) { Tg[(size_t)i + (size_t)i * NBMAX] = taus[i]; taub[p + i] = taus[i]; }
1137	    __syncthreads();
1138	    for (int l = 1; l < nb; ++l) {
1139	        const float* Vl = Ps + (size_t)l * ldp;
1140	        float pz[NBMAX];
1141	        #pragma unroll
1142	        for (int t = 0; t < NBMAX; ++t) pz[t] = 0.f;
1143	        for (int rr = l + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) {
1144	            float vl = (rr == l) ? 1.f : Vl[rr];
1145	            for (int i = 0; i < l; ++i) {
1146	                const float* Vi = Ps + (size_t)i * ldp;
1147	                float vi = (rr == i) ? 1.f : Vi[rr];
1148	                pz[i] += vi * vl;
1149	            }
1150	        }
1151	        for (int i = 0; i < l; ++i) {
1152	            float v = pz[i];
1153	            #pragma unroll
1154	            for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) v += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, v, o);
1155	            if (lane == 0) red[i * NWARP + warp] = v;
1156	        }
1157	        __syncthreads();
1158	        if (tid < l) {
1159	            float zz = 0.f;
1160	            for (int wi = 0; wi < NWARP; ++wi) zz += red[tid * NWARP + wi];
1161	            zsh[tid] = zz;
1162	        }
1163	        __syncthreads();
1164	        float tl = taus[l];
1165	        for (int i = tid; i < l; i += TPB) {
1166	            float acc = 0.f;
1167	            for (int m = i; m < l; ++m) acc += Tg[(size_t)i + (size_t)m * NBMAX] * zsh[m];
1168	            Tg[(size_t)i + (size_t)l * NBMAX] = -tl * acc;
1169	        }
1170	        __syncthreads();
1171	    }
1172	    for (int idx = tid; idx < ldp * nb; idx += TPB) {
1173	        int j = idx / ldp, rr = idx % ldp;
1174	        Acm[(size_t)(p + j) * n + (p + rr)] = Ps[rr + j * ldp];
1175	    }
1176	}
1177	
1178	// TRAILING kernel: grid-strides over (matrix b, column-tile g0) work items.
1179	// Small smem (Ts + Ws + Wps + Vs) -> high occupancy, large grid. For each work
1180	// item applies the block reflector to CT trailing columns of matrix b:
1181	//   W = V^T C ; W' = T^T W ; C -= V W'  (V staged through smem in RB-row strips).
1182	template <int TPB, int NBMAX, int CT, int RB>
1183	__global__ void qr_trailing_kernel(float* __restrict__ Acm_all, const float* __restrict__ Tg_all,
1184	                                   int B, int n, int p, int nb) {
1185	    extern __shared__ float dsmem[];
1186	    float* Ts  = dsmem;                       // nb*nb
1187	    float* Ws  = Ts + (size_t)NBMAX * NBMAX;  // nb*CT
1188	    float* Wps = Ws + (size_t)NBMAX * CT;     // nb*CT
1189	    float* Vs  = Wps + (size_t)NBMAX * CT;    // RB*nb
1190	    float* Cs  = Vs + (size_t)RB * NBMAX;     // RB*CT (C strip, col-major Cs[rr+g*RB])
1191	    const int tid = threadIdx.x;
1192	
1193	    const int tstart = p + nb;
1194	    const int ntiles = (n - tstart + CT - 1) / CT;   // column tiles per matrix
1195	    if (ntiles <= 0) return;
1196	    const long totwork = (long)B * ntiles;
1197	
1198	    for (long widx = blockIdx.x; widx < totwork; widx += gridDim.x) {
1199	        int b = widx / ntiles;
1200	        int tileIdx = widx - (long)b * ntiles;
1201	        int g0 = tstart + tileIdx * CT;
1202	        int ct = CT; if (g0 + ct > n) ct = n - g0;
1203	        float* Acm = Acm_all + (size_t)b * n * n;
1204	        const float* Tg = Tg_all + (size_t)b * NBMAX * NBMAX;
1205	
1206	        // cache T for this matrix
1207	        for (int idx = tid; idx < nb * nb; idx += TPB) Ts[idx] = Tg[idx % nb + (idx / nb) * NBMAX];
1208	        __syncthreads();
1209	
1210	        // pass 1: W = V^T C. Stage BOTH V and C strips into smem so each C
1211	        // element is read from global ONCE per strip (was read nb times).
1212	        for (int idx = tid; idx < nb * ct; idx += TPB) Ws[idx] = 0.f;
1213	        __syncthreads();
1214	        for (int r0 = p; r0 < n; r0 += RB) {
1215	            int rb = RB; if (r0 + rb > n) rb = n - r0;
1216	            for (int idx = tid; idx < rb * nb; idx += TPB) {
1217	                int i = idx / rb, rr = idx % rb, r = r0 + rr, ci = p + i;
1218	                float vv = (r < ci) ? 0.f : (r == ci ? 1.f : Acm[(size_t)ci * n + r]);
1219	                Vs[rr + i * RB] = vv;
1220	            }
1221	            for (int idx = tid; idx < rb * ct; idx += TPB) {
1222	                int g = idx / rb, rr = idx % rb;
1223	                Cs[rr + g * RB] = Acm[(size_t)(g0 + g) * n + (r0 + rr)];
1224	            }
1225	            __syncthreads();
1226	            for (int idx = tid; idx < nb * ct; idx += TPB) {
1227	                int g = idx / nb, i = idx % nb;
1228	                float acc = 0.f;
1229	                for (int rr = 0; rr < rb; ++rr) acc += Vs[rr + i * RB] * Cs[rr + g * RB];
1230	                Ws[i + g * nb] += acc;
1231	            }
1232	            __syncthreads();
1233	        }
1234	        // W' = -T^T W
1235	        for (int idx = tid; idx < nb * ct; idx += TPB) {
1236	            int g = idx / nb, i = idx % nb;
1237	            float acc = 0.f;

1323	// TWO-LEVEL panel for the batched scheme: factor a WIDE panel of width NB using
1324	// inner sub-blocks of width IB (each held in smem at (n-ps)*IB, which fits even
1325	// when (n-p)*NB would not). This decouples the trailing block width NB (which we
1326	// want LARGE -> the trailing update re-reads C n/NB times, so HBM traffic ~1/NB)
1327	// from the smem limit. The panel kernel still runs B blocks, so its cost is on
1328	// B SMs; the wide T is built from the global reflectors. The same trailing
1329	// kernel then runs with the large NB.
1330	// ===========================================================================
1331	
1332	// Factor inner sub-block [ps,ps+ib) (cols local 0..ib-1) of matrix Acm, holding
1333	// rows[ps,n) x ib in smem Ps; write reflectors+R back to Acm; fill the IB-block
1334	// diagonal of the wide T (Tg col-major, NBMAX-leading) at columns [ps-p..].
1335	template <int TPB, int IB, int NBMAX>
1336	__device__ void wpanel_inner_factor(float* __restrict__ Acm, float* __restrict__ Tg,
1337	                                    float* __restrict__ taub, float* Ps,
1338	                                    float* red, float* sval, float* zsh, float* taus,
1339	                                    int n, int p, int ps, int ib) {
1340	    const int NWARP = TPB / 32;
1341	    const int tid = threadIdx.x;
1342	    const int lane = tid & 31, warp = tid >> 5;
1343	    const int ldp = n - ps;
1344	    for (int idx = tid; idx < ldp * ib; idx += TPB) {
1345	        int j = idx / ldp, rr = idx % ldp;
1346	        Ps[rr + j * ldp] = Acm[(size_t)(ps + j) * n + (ps + rr)];
1347	    }
1348	    __syncthreads();
1349	    for (int j = 0; j < ib; ++j) {
1350	        float* pj = Ps + (size_t)j * ldp;
1351	        int rj = j;
1352	        float partial = 0.f;
1353	        for (int rr = rj + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) { float x = pj[rr]; partial += x * x; }
1354	        red[tid] = partial; __syncthreads();
1355	        for (int s = TPB / 2; s > 0; s >>= 1) { if (tid < s) red[tid] += red[tid + s]; __syncthreads(); }
1356	        if (tid == 0) {
1357	            float xnorm = sqrtf(red[0]);
1358	            float alpha = pj[rj];
1359	            float beta = (alpha >= 0.f) ? -xnorm : xnorm;
1360	            float tval, invden;
1361	            if (xnorm > 0.f && (alpha - beta) != 0.f) { tval = (beta - alpha) / beta; invden = 1.f / (alpha - beta); }
1362	            else { tval = 0.f; invden = 0.f; beta = alpha; }
1363	            sval[0] = beta; sval[1] = tval; sval[2] = invden;
1364	        }
1365	        __syncthreads();
1366	        float beta = sval[0], tval = sval[1], invden = sval[2];
1367	        for (int rr = rj + 1 + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) pj[rr] *= invden;
1368	        __syncthreads();
1369	        if (tid == 0) { pj[rj] = 1.f; taus[j] = tval; }
1370	        __syncthreads();
1371	        int ntrail = ib - (j + 1);
1372	        if (ntrail > 0) {
1373	            float pw[IB];
1374	            #pragma unroll
1375	            for (int t = 0; t < IB; ++t) pw[t] = 0.f;
1376	            for (int rr = rj + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) {

1378	                for (int t = 0; t < ntrail; ++t) pw[t] += vr * Ps[(size_t)(j + 1 + t) * ldp + rr];
1379	            }
1380	            for (int t = 0; t < ntrail; ++t) {
1381	                float v = pw[t];
1382	                #pragma unroll
1383	                for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) v += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, v, o);
1384	                if (lane == 0) red[t * NWARP + warp] = v;
1385	            }
1386	            __syncthreads();
1387	            if (tid < ntrail) { float w = 0.f; for (int wi = 0; wi < NWARP; ++wi) w += red[tid * NWARP + wi]; zsh[tid] = tval * w; }
1388	            __syncthreads();
1389	            for (int t = 0; t < ntrail; ++t) {
1390	                float tw = zsh[t];
1391	                float* pjj = Ps + (size_t)(j + 1 + t) * ldp;
1392	                for (int rr = rj + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) pjj[rr] -= tw * pj[rr];
1393	            }
1394	            __syncthreads();
1395	        }
1396	        if (tid == 0) pj[rj] = beta;
1397	        __syncthreads();
1398	    }
1399	    // diagonal IB-block of wide T (recurrence within the inner block, V from smem)
1400	    int co = ps - p;     // wide-column offset of this inner block
1401	    for (int i = tid; i < ib; i += TPB) { Tg[(size_t)(co + i) + (size_t)(co + i) * NBMAX] = taus[i]; taub[ps + i] = taus[i]; }
1402	    __syncthreads();
1403	    for (int l = 1; l < ib; ++l) {
1404	        const float* Vl = Ps + (size_t)l * ldp;
1405	        float pz[IB];
1406	        #pragma unroll
1407	        for (int t = 0; t < IB; ++t) pz[t] = 0.f;
1408	        for (int rr = l + tid; rr < ldp; rr += TPB) {
1409	            float vl = (rr == l) ? 1.f : Vl[rr];
1410	            for (int i = 0; i < l; ++i) { const float* Vi = Ps + (size_t)i * ldp; float vi = (rr == i) ? 1.f : Vi[rr]; pz[i] += vi * vl; }
1411	        }
1412	        for (int i = 0; i < l; ++i) { float v = pz[i]; for (int o = 16; o > 0; o >>= 1) v += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, v, o); if (lane == 0) red[i * NWARP + warp] = v; }
1413	        __syncthreads();
1414	        if (tid < l) { float zz = 0.f; for (int wi = 0; wi < NWARP; ++wi) zz += red[tid * NWARP + wi]; zsh[tid] = zz; }
1415	        __syncthreads();
1416	        float tl = taus[l];
1417	        for (int i = tid; i < l; i += TPB) {
1418	            float acc = 0.f;
1419	            for (int m = i; m < l; ++m) acc += Tg[(size_t)(co + i) + (size_t)(co + m) * NBMAX] * zsh[m];
1420	            Tg[(size_t)(co + i) + (size_t)(co + l) * NBMAX] = -tl * acc;
1421	        }
1422	        __syncthreads();
1423	    }

1425	    for (int idx = tid; idx < ldp * ib; idx += TPB) {

1433	// [ps,ps+ib), rows>=ps, implicit unit diag) to wide-panel columns [c0,c1) in
1434	// global Acm: C -= V (Tib^T (V^T C)). Tib is the IB-diagonal block of Tg.

1436	template <int TPB, int IB, int NBMAX, int RB>
1437	__device__ void wpanel_apply_inner(float* __restrict__ Acm, const float* __restrict__ Tg,
1438	                                   float* Wbuf, float* Vbuf, float* Tib,
1439	                                   int n, int p, int ps, int ib, int c0, int c1) {

1441	    int wcols = c1 - c0;
1442	    if (wcols <= 0) return;
1443	    int co = ps - p;
1444	    // cache Tib (ib x ib upper-tri) contiguous Tib[l + i*ib]
1445	    for (int idx = tid; idx < ib * ib; idx += TPB) Tib[idx] = Tg[(size_t)(co + idx % ib) + (size_t)(co + idx / ib) * NBMAX];

1447	    // W = V^T C  (ib x wcols)
1448	    for (int idx = tid; idx < ib * wcols; idx += TPB) Wbuf[idx] = 0.f;
1449	    __syncthreads();
1450	    for (int r0 = ps; r0 < n; r0 += RB) {
1451	        int rb = RB; if (r0 + rb > n) rb = n - r0;
1452	        for (int idx = tid; idx < rb * ib; idx += TPB) {
1453	            int i = idx / rb, rr = idx % rb, r = r0 + rr, ci = ps + i;

But my coop2 is a hand-written CUDA kernel using mma/tensor cores would require manual tf32x3 (split each FP32 into 2-3 TF32 components). That's complex. 

The key strategic decision: **My coop2 trailing GEMM is hand-written CUDA. Worker-2 already has a complete Triton trailing GEMM with tf32x3.** The brief says "REUSE its approach rather than reinventing it" and "put a tf32x3 tensor-core trailing GEMM into your coop2 trailing_kernel."

The cleanest, highest-leverage path: **Replace my coop2 `qr_trailing_kernel` (CUDA SIMT GEMM) with a Triton tf32x3 trailing update**, keeping my CUDA panel factor (which is fast and exact). This is a hybrid: CUDA panel + Triton tf32x3 trailing. Let me read worker-2's full trailing kernels and the parent profile to ground the decision.

8	# Batch-MAJOR right-looking blocked Householder QR (geqrf-compatible).
9	#
10	# For a panel of width b starting at column j:
11	#   1. panel_factor : one program per matrix factors A[j:, j:j+b] in place
12	#      (b unblocked Householder steps, panel resident in registers/SMEM),
13	#      producing reflectors V (unit lower-trapezoidal) and tau.
14	#   2. build_T      : per matrix, form the b x b WY T factor from V and tau.
15	#   3. trailing     : A[j:, j+b:] := (I - V T^T V^T) A[j:, j+b:]  (BLAS-3).
16	#
17	# H upper-tri = R, below-diag = reflectors, tau separate. FP32 throughout.
18	# Verified bit-equivalent to torch.geqrf in a PyTorch prototype.
19	# =============================================================================
20	
21	
22	@triton.jit
23	def _panel_factor_kernel(
24	    A_ptr, tau_ptr, Vbuf_ptr, Tbuf_ptr,
25	    B, N, j, pheight, b,
26	    stride_ab, stride_an,
27	    stride_vb, stride_vk, stride_vn,
28	    stride_tb, stride_tk, stride_tn,
29	    BLK: tl.constexpr, MAXH: tl.constexpr,
30	):
31	    bid = tl.program_id(0)
32	    if bid >= B:
33	        return
34	
35	    rows = tl.arange(0, MAXH)                 # relative to panel top (global row j)
36	    cols = tl.arange(0, BLK)
37	    row_valid = rows < pheight
38	    col_valid = cols < b
39	
40	    a_base = A_ptr + bid * stride_ab + j * stride_an + j
41	    aptr = a_base + rows[:, None] * stride_an + cols[None, :]
42	    mask = row_valid[:, None] & col_valid[None, :]
43	    panel = tl.load(aptr, mask=mask, other=0.0)          # (MAXH, BLK)
44	
45	    tau_panel = tl.zeros((BLK,), dtype=tl.float32)
46	    # Build the WY T factor (BLK x BLK upper-tri) incrementally here (LAPACK
47	    # dlarft forward): at step k, T[0:k,k] = -tau_k * T[0:k,0:k] * (V[:,0:k]^T v_k).
48	    # This fuses build_T into panel_factor, eliminating a whole low-occupancy
49	    # kernel launch + a re-read of V from HBM.
50	    Tmat = tl.zeros((BLK, BLK), dtype=tl.float32)
51	
52	    for k in range(0, BLK):
53	        do_k = k < b
54	        col_is_k = cols == k
55	        xk = tl.sum(tl.where(col_is_k[None, :], panel, 0.0), axis=1)   # (MAXH,)
56	        active = (rows >= k) & row_valid
57	        xk = tl.where(active, xk, 0.0)
58	
59	        alpha = tl.sum(tl.where(rows == k, xk, 0.0))
60	        tailv = tl.where(rows > k, xk, 0.0)
61	        tail_n2 = tl.sum(tailv * tailv)
62	        normx = tl.sqrt(alpha * alpha + tail_n2)
63	        sgn = tl.where(alpha >= 0.0, 1.0, -1.0)
64	        beta = -sgn * normx
65	        has_refl = tail_n2 > 0.0
66	        beta_safe = tl.where(beta == 0.0, 1.0, beta)
67	        tau_k = tl.where(has_refl, (beta - alpha) / beta_safe, 0.0)
68	
69	        denom = alpha - beta
70	        denom = tl.where(denom == 0.0, 1.0, denom)
71	        v = tl.where(rows > k, xk / denom, 0.0)
72	        v = tl.where(rows == k, 1.0, v)
73	        v = tl.where(active, v, 0.0)
74	        v = tl.where(has_refl, v, tl.where(rows == k, 1.0, 0.0))
75	
76	        # w[c] = v_k . panel[:,c] -- used both for the trailing-panel update AND
77	        # the incremental T factor. Because v_k is supported only on rows >= k,
78	        # for c < k we have z[c] = V[:,c].v_k == w[c] exactly (the diagonal/above
79	        # terms vanish), so the WY recurrence needs no separate (MAXH,BLK) Vmat
80	        # tensor or extra reduction -- a big register/occupancy win on the panel.
81	        w = tl.sum(v[:, None] * panel, axis=0)            # (BLK,)
82	
83	        # --- incremental T column k:  T[a<k,k] = -tau_k * (T @ w[c<k]) ---
84	        z = tl.where(cols < k, w, 0.0)
85	        Tcol = -tau_k * tl.sum(Tmat * z[None, :], axis=1)  # (BLK,)
86	        Tcol = tl.where(cols < k, Tcol, 0.0)

88	        Tmat = tl.where(col_is_k[None, :], Tcol[:, None], Tmat)
89	
90	        # apply H_k to trailing panel columns (c > k)
91	        upd = tau_k * v[:, None] * w[None, :]
92	        col_gt_k = cols > k
93	        panel = tl.where(col_gt_k[None, :], panel - upd, panel)
94	
95	        # store this column: R[k,k] on diag, reflector below; leave rows<k
96	        # (already-finalized R entries from earlier steps) untouched.
97	        diagval = tl.where(has_refl, beta, alpha)
98	        new_colk = tl.where(rows == k, diagval, v)        # row==k -> beta, row>k -> v
99	        panel = tl.where(col_is_k[None, :] & (rows[:, None] >= k), new_colk[:, None], panel)

101	        tau_panel = tl.where(col_is_k & do_k, tau_k, tau_panel)

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl
from task import input_t, output_t


# =============================================================================
# Batch-MAJOR right-looking blocked Householder QR (geqrf-compatible).
#
# For a panel of width b starting at column j:
#   1. panel_factor : one program per matrix factors A[j:, j:j+b] in place
#      (b unblocked Householder steps, panel resident in registers/SMEM),
#      producing reflectors V (unit lower-trapezoidal) and tau.
#   2. build_T      : per matrix, form the b x b WY T factor from V and tau.
#   3. trailing     : A[j:, j+b:] := (I - V T^T V^T) A[j:, j+b:]  (BLAS-3).
#
# H upper-tri = R, below-diag = reflectors, tau separate. FP32 throughout.
# Verified bit-equivalent to torch.geqrf in a PyTorch prototype.
# =============================================================================


@triton.jit
def _panel_factor_kernel(
    A_ptr, tau_ptr, Vbuf_ptr, Tbuf_ptr,
    B, N, j, pheight, b,
    stride_ab, stride_an,
    stride_vb, stride_vk, stride_vn,
    stride_tb, stride_tk, stride_tn,
    BLK: tl.constexpr, MAXH: tl.constexpr,
):
    bid = tl.program_id(0)
    if bid >= B:
        return

    rows = tl.arange(0, MAXH)                 # relative to panel top (global row j)
    cols = tl.arange(0, BLK)
    row_valid = rows < pheight
    col_valid = cols < b

    a_base = A_ptr + bid * stride_ab + j * stride_an + j
    aptr = a_base + rows[:, None] * stride_an + cols[None, :]
    mask = row_valid[:, None] & col_valid[None, :]
    panel = tl.load(aptr, mask=mask, other=0.0)          # (MAXH, BLK)

    tau_panel = tl.zeros((BLK,), dtype=tl.float32)
    # Build the WY T factor (BLK x BLK upper-tri) incrementally here (LAPACK
    # dlarft forward): at step k, T[0:k,k] = -tau_k * T[0:k,0:k] * (V[:,0:k]^T v_k).
    # This fuses build_T into panel_factor, eliminating a whole low-occupancy
    # kernel launch + a re-read of V from HBM.
    Tmat = tl.zeros((BLK, BLK), dtype=tl.float32)

    for k in range(0, BLK):
        do_k = k < b
        col_is_k = cols == k
        xk = tl.sum(tl.where(col_is_k[None, :], panel, 0.0), axis=1)   # (MAXH,)
        active = (rows >= k) & row_valid
        xk = tl.where(active, xk, 0.0)

        alpha = tl.sum(tl.where(rows == k, xk, 0.0))
        tailv = tl.where(rows > k, xk, 0.0)
        tail_n2 = tl.sum(tailv * tailv)
        normx = tl.sqrt(alpha * alpha + tail_n2)
        sgn = tl.where(alpha >= 0.0, 1.0, -1.0)
        beta = -sgn * normx
        has_refl = tail_n2 > 0.0
        beta_safe = tl.where(beta == 0.0, 1.0, beta)
        tau_k = tl.where(has_refl, (beta - alpha) / beta_safe, 0.0)

        denom = alpha - beta
        denom = tl.where(denom == 0.0, 1.0, denom)
        v = tl.where(rows > k, xk / denom, 0.0)
        v = tl.where(rows == k, 1.0, v)
        v = tl.where(active, v, 0.0)
        v = tl.where(has_refl, v, tl.where(rows == k, 1.0, 0.0))

        # w[c] = v_k . panel[:,c] -- used both for the trailing-panel update AND
        # the incremental T factor. Because v_k is supported only on rows >= k,
        # for c < k we have z[c] = V[:,c].v_k == w[c] exactly (the diagonal/above
        # terms vanish), so the WY recurrence needs no separate (MAXH,BLK) Vmat
        # tensor or extra reduction -- a big register/occupancy win on the panel.
        w = tl.sum(v[:, None] * panel, axis=0)            # (BLK,)

        # --- incremental T column k:  T[a<k,k] = -tau_k * (T @ w[c<k]) ---
        z = tl.where(cols < k, w, 0.0)
        Tcol = -tau_k * tl.sum(Tmat * z[None, :], axis=1)  # (BLK,)
        Tcol = tl.where(cols < k, Tcol, 0.0)
        Tcol = tl.where(cols == k, tau_k, Tcol)
        Tmat = tl.where(col_is_k[None, :], Tcol[:, None], Tmat)

        # apply H_k to trailing panel columns (c > k)
        upd = tau_k * v[:, None] * w[None, :]
        col_gt_k = cols > k
        panel = tl.where(col_gt_k[None, :], panel - upd, panel)

        # store this column: R[k,k] on diag, reflector below; leave rows<k
        # (already-finalized R entries from earlier steps) untouched.
        diagval = tl.where(has_refl, beta, alpha)
        new_colk = tl.where(rows == k, diagval, v)        # row==k -> beta, row>k -> v
        panel = tl.where(col_is_k[None, :] & (rows[:, None] >= k), new_colk[:, None], panel)

        tau_panel = tl.where(col_is_k & do_k, tau_k, tau_panel)

    tl.store(aptr, panel, mask=mask)

    tptr = tau_ptr + bid * N + j + cols
    tl.store(tptr, tau_panel, mask=col_valid)

    # V transposed: Vt[c, r] = 1 if r==c, panel[r,c] if r>c, else 0
    panelT = tl.trans(panel)                               # (BLK, MAXH)
    cc = cols[:, None]
    rr = rows[None, :]
    Vt = tl.where(rr == cc, 1.0, tl.where(rr > cc, panelT, 0.0))
    Vt = tl.where((rr < pheight) & (cc < b), Vt, 0.0)
    vbase = Vbuf_ptr + bid * stride_vb
    vptr = vbase + cc * stride_vk + rr * stride_vn
    tl.store(vptr, Vt, mask=(rr < pheight) & (cc < b))

    # store T
    tbase = Tbuf_ptr + bid * stride_tb
    tptr2 = tbase + cols[:, None] * stride_tk + cols[None, :] * stride_tn
    tl.store(tptr2, Tmat)


# Trailing update is split into TWO kernels to be race-free: the first reads
# A_trail and produces YT = T^T V^T A_trail (read-only consumer of A_trail); the
# second reads YT (read-only) and applies A_trail -= V @ YT (each program owns a
# disjoint output tile). Fusing them (one kernel that both reads all rows of a
# column and writes its own row slice) races: program for row-tile r0 reads rows
# owned by row-tile r1 while r1 writes them.
@triton.jit
def _trailing_YT_kernel(
    A_ptr, Vbuf_ptr, Tbuf_ptr, YT_ptr,
    B, N, j, pheight, ncols, jb,
    stride_ab, stride_an,
    stride_vb, stride_vk, stride_vn,
    stride_tb, stride_tk, stride_tn,
    stride_yb, stride_yk, stride_yn,
    BLK: tl.constexpr, BM: tl.constexpr, BNc: tl.constexpr,
):
    col_tile = tl.program_id(0)
    bid = tl.program_id(1)
    if bid >= B:
        return
    c0 = col_tile * BNc
    ccols = c0 + tl.arange(0, BNc)
    cmask = ccols < ncols
    krange = tl.arange(0, BLK)

    a_trail_base = A_ptr + bid * stride_ab + j * stride_an + jb
    v_base = Vbuf_ptr + bid * stride_vb

    # W = V^T @ A_trail over all panel rows, in chunks of BM
    W = tl.zeros((BLK, BNc), dtype=tl.float32)
    nchunks = tl.cdiv(pheight, BM)
    for ci in range(0, nchunks):
        rr = ci * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
        rrmask = rr < pheight
        ap = a_trail_base + rr[:, None] * stride_an + ccols[None, :]
        achunk = tl.load(ap, mask=rrmask[:, None] & cmask[None, :], other=0.0)   # (BM,BNc)
        vp = v_base + krange[:, None] * stride_vk + rr[None, :] * stride_vn
        vchunk = tl.load(vp, mask=rrmask[None, :], other=0.0)                    # (BLK,BM)
        W += tl.dot(vchunk, achunk, input_precision="tf32x3")

    # YT = T^T @ W
    tp = Tbuf_ptr + bid * stride_tb + krange[:, None] * stride_tk + krange[None, :] * stride_tn
    Tm = tl.load(tp)
    YT = tl.dot(tl.trans(Tm), W, input_precision="tf32x3")                        # (BLK,BNc)

    yp = YT_ptr + bid * stride_yb + krange[:, None] * stride_yk + ccols[None, :] * stride_yn
    tl.store(yp, YT, mask=cmask[None, :])


@triton.jit
def _trailing_apply_kernel(
    A_ptr, Vbuf_ptr, YT_ptr,
    B, N, j, pheight, ncols, jb,
    stride_ab, stride_an,
    stride_vb, stride_vk, stride_vn,
    stride_yb, stride_yk, stride_yn,
    BLK: tl.constexpr, BM: tl.constexpr, BNc: tl.constexpr,
):
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    bid = tl.program_id(1)
    if bid >= B:
        return
    num_col_tiles = tl.cdiv(ncols, BNc)
    row_tile = pid // num_col_tiles
    col_tile = pid % num_col_tiles
    rrows = row_tile * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
    ccols = col_tile * BNc + tl.arange(0, BNc)
    rmask = rrows < pheight
    cmask = ccols < ncols
    krange = tl.arange(0, BLK)

    a_trail_base = A_ptr + bid * stride_ab + j * stride_an + jb
    v_base = Vbuf_ptr + bid * stride_vb

    # V[rrows,:] : (BM, BLK)
    vp = v_base + krange[None, :] * stride_vk + rrows[:, None] * stride_vn
    Vrow = tl.load(vp, mask=rmask[:, None], other=0.0)
    # YT[:, ccols] : (BLK, BNc)
    yp = YT_ptr + bid * stride_yb + krange[:, None] * stride_yk + ccols[None, :] * stride_yn
    YT = tl.load(yp, mask=cmask[None, :], other=0.0)
    delta = tl.dot(Vrow, YT, input_precision="tf32x3")                            # (BM,BNc)

    ap = a_trail_base + rrows[:, None] * stride_an + ccols[None, :]
    amask = rmask[:, None] & cmask[None, :]
    aorig = tl.load(ap, mask=amask, other=0.0)
    tl.store(ap, aorig - delta, mask=amask)


def custom_kernel(data: input_t) -> output_t:
    A = data
    B, N, _ = A.shape
    H = A.clone()
    tau = torch.zeros((B, N), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)

    if N <= 32:
        BLK = min(16, N)
    elif N >= 1536:
        # Tall panels (n>=2048): a narrow block halves the panel register
        # footprint -> much higher occupancy (~2x faster) than BLK=32.
        BLK = 16
    else:
        BLK = 32

    Vbuf = torch.empty((B, BLK, N), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    Tbuf = torch.empty((B, BLK, BLK), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    YTbuf = torch.empty((B, BLK, N), device=A.device, dtype=torch.float32)

    sab, san = H.stride(0), H.stride(1)
    svb, svk, svn = Vbuf.stride(0), Vbuf.stride(1), Vbuf.stride(2)
    stb, stk, stn = Tbuf.stride(0), Tbuf.stride(1), Tbuf.stride(2)
    syb, syk, syn = YTbuf.stride(0), YTbuf.stride(1), YTbuf.stride(2)

    # Trailing-update tiles, tuned per-kernel via micro-sweep on the dominant
    # B=640 n=512 panel (tf32x3, BLK=32 rank):
    #   YT (W=V^T@A reduces over tall pheight, BLK=32 output rows): small tile +
    #       1 warp wins (205us vs parent 216us) -- tiny output, 1-warp latency.
    #   apply (delta=Vrow@YT, disjoint output tiles): TALL-NARROW BM=128,BNc=32
    #       + 4 warps wins (333us vs parent 395us, -16%). Keeping BNc==BLK==32
    #       avoids K-starving the K=32 MMA; tall BM reuses the loaded YT across
    #       many rows. (Bigger BNc regressed: K=32 << BNc starves the tensor core.)
    BM_Y, BNc_Y, NW_Y = 32, 32, 1
    BM_A, BNc_A, NW_A = 128, 32, 4
    j = 0
    while j < N:
        b = min(BLK, N - j)
        pheight = N - j
        MAXH = triton.next_power_of_2(pheight)

        # num_warps must scale with the panel height: the panel kernel holds a
        # (MAXH, BLK) register tensor; too few warps -> register spill -> huge
        # slowdown (measured 7-10x on n>=1024). Empirically-tuned per MAXH.
        if MAXH <= 512:
            nwp = 4
        elif MAXH <= 1024:
            nwp = 8
        else:
            nwp = 32

        _panel_factor_kernel[(B,)](
            H, tau, Vbuf, Tbuf,
            B, N, j, pheight, b,
            sab, san, svb, svk, svn, stb, stk, stn,
            BLK=BLK, MAXH=MAXH, num_warps=nwp,
        )

        ncols = N - (j + b)
        if ncols > 0:
            nct_y = triton.cdiv(ncols, BNc_Y)
            _trailing_YT_kernel[(nct_y, B)](
                H, Vbuf, Tbuf, YTbuf,
                B, N, j, pheight, ncols, j + b,
                sab, san, svb, svk, svn, stb, stk, stn, syb, syk, syn,
                BLK=BLK, BM=BM_Y, BNc=BNc_Y, num_warps=NW_Y,
            )
            nct_a = triton.cdiv(ncols, BNc_A)
            nrt_a = triton.cdiv(pheight, BM_A)
            _trailing_apply_kernel[(nrt_a * nct_a, B)](
                H, Vbuf, YTbuf,
                B, N, j, pheight, ncols, j + b,
                sab, san, svb, svk, svn, syb, syk, syn,
                BLK=BLK, BM=BM_A, BNc=BNc_A, num_warps=NW_A,
            )
        j += b

    return H, tau

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl
from task import input_t, output_t


# =============================================================================
# TENSOR-CORE (tf32x3) trailing update for the coop2 batched QR.
#
# The coop2 trailing kernel was an FP32-SIMT GEMM and ran at ~1 TFLOP/s --
# 85% of total GPU time at n=512 (memory-bound, no tensor cores). These Triton
# kernels replace it with a tf32x3 ERROR-CORRECTED tensor-core block-reflector
# update:  C -= V (T^T (V^T C)).  tf32x3 (Triton's input_precision) splits each
# FP32 operand into TF32 hi + residual and accumulates the 3 dominant
# cross-products, recovering ~FP32 accuracy (verified to pass every
# ill-conditioned case where plain 1-pass TF32 fails the 20*n*eps factor gate).
#
# These operate DIRECTLY on the coop2 column-major scratch Acm (viewed as a
# (B,n,n) tensor Acm[b,c,r] == element row r, col c) and the compact-WY T
# (Tg[b,l,i] == T[i,l], upper-tri).  Reflectors V live in-place below the
# diagonal of Acm cols [p,p+nb) with implicit unit diagonal (the stored diag
# holds R's beta), exactly as the CUDA panel kernel left them -- no separate V
# buffer or transpose is needed.  Split into TWO kernels (YT producer / apply
# consumer) so the apply step's disjoint output tiles never race the reads.
# =============================================================================

@triton.jit
def _coop_trailing_YT_cm(
    Acm_ptr, Tg_ptr, YT_ptr,
    B, n, p, nb, ncols, jb,
    s_ab, s_ac, s_ar,            # Acm[b,c,r] strides
    s_tb, s_tl, s_ti,            # Tg[b,l,i] strides
    s_yb, s_yk, s_yc,            # YT[b,k,c] strides
    BLK: tl.constexpr, BM: tl.constexpr, BNc: tl.constexpr,
):
    # YT[i, g] = sum_{l<=i} T[l,i] * (sum_{r>=p} V[r,l] * C[r,g])
    # for trailing columns g in a BNc-wide tile, all nb reflector rows i.
    col_tile = tl.program_id(0)
    bid = tl.program_id(1)
    if bid >= B:
        return
    c0 = col_tile * BNc
    gcols = jb + c0 + tl.arange(0, BNc)        # global trailing column indices
    gvalid = (c0 + tl.arange(0, BNc)) < ncols

# Trailing-update tile shapes for the Triton tf32x3 kernels (mirrors worker-2's
# tuned per-kernel micro-sweep on the dominant B=640 n=512 panel):
#   YT (W=V^T@C reduces over tall pheight, BLK output rows): small tile + 1 warp.
#   apply (delta=Vrow@YT, disjoint output tiles): TALL-NARROW BM=128, BNc=32, 4w
#   (K=BLK pins BNc==BLK so the MMA's K dim isn't starved by a wide BNc).

def _qr_cuda_coop2_tc(a: torch.Tensor, nb: int = 0) -> output_t:
    # coop2 with a TENSOR-CORE (tf32x3) trailing update. The CUDA panel kernel
    # (exact FP32 Householder + compact-WY T, on-chip) and transposes are kept;
    # only the trailing block-reflector update -- 85% of GPU time and previously
    # an FP32-SIMT ~1 TFLOP/s GEMM -- is replaced with two Triton tf32x3 tl.dot
    # kernels reading the column-major Acm in place. The Python loop alternates
    # CUDA panel -> Triton trailing; each kernel launch is the cross-CTA barrier.
    B, n, _ = a.shape
    if nb <= 0:
        nb = _coop_nb(n)
    H = torch.empty_like(a)
    Acm = torch.empty((B, n, n), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    Tg = torch.empty((B, nb, nb), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    tau = torch.empty((B, n), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    YT = torch.empty((B, nb, n), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    mod = _get_cuda_mod()

    s_ab, s_ac, s_ar = Acm.stride(0), Acm.stride(1), Acm.stride(2)
    s_tb, s_tl, s_ti = Tg.stride(0), Tg.stride(1), Tg.stride(2)
    s_yb, s_yk, s_yc = YT.stride(0), YT.stride(1), YT.stride(2)
    BM_Y, BNc_Y, NW_Y = _TC_YT
    BM_A, BNc_A, NW_A = _TC_APPLY

    mod.qr_coop2_transpose_in(a.data_ptr(), Acm.data_ptr(), B, n)
    p = 0
    while p < n:
        cur_nb = nb if p + nb <= n else n - p
        mod.qr_coop2_panel(Acm.data_ptr(), Tg.data_ptr(), tau.data_ptr(),
                           B, n, nb, p, cur_nb)
        jb = p + cur_nb
        ncols = n - jb
        if ncols > 0:
            nct_y = triton.cdiv(ncols, BNc_Y)
            _coop_trailing_YT_cm[(nct_y, B)](
                Acm, Tg, YT,
                B, n, p, cur_nb, ncols, jb,
                s_ab, s_ac, s_ar, s_tb, s_tl, s_ti, s_yb, s_yk, s_yc,
                BLK=nb, BM=BM_Y, BNc=BNc_Y, num_warps=NW_Y,
            )
            nct_a = triton.cdiv(ncols, BNc_A)
            nrt_a = triton.cdiv(n - p, BM_A)
            _coop_trailing_apply_cm[(nrt_a * nct_a, B)](
                Acm, YT,
                B, n, p, cur_nb, ncols, jb,
                s_ab, s_ac, s_ar, s_yb, s_yk, s_yc,
                BLK=nb, BM=BM_A, BNc=BNc_A, num_warps=NW_A,
            )
        p += cur_nb
    mod.qr_coop2_transpose_out(Acm.data_ptr(), H.data_ptr(), B, n)
    return H, tau

Now let me debug. The residuals being huge (not just tf32 noise) means the block reflector update is mathematically wrong. Let me reason carefully about each potential bug:

1. **`s_ac` vs `s_ar` interpretation**: `Acm` is shape `(B, n, n)` row-major contiguous → `Acm[b, c, r]` with strides `(n*n, n, 1)`. So `s_ab=n*n, s_ac=n, s_ar=1`. Element (row r, col c) at `Acm.data[b*n*n + c*n + r]`. ✓ Correct.

2. **V loading**: V[r, i] for reflector i = global col `p+i`. `V[r,i] = Acm[b, p+i, r]`. In YT kernel I load `vp = base + vcols[:,None]*s_ac + rr[None,:]*s_ar` where `vcols = p + krange`. So `vp[i, m] = base + (p+i)*s_ac + rr[m]*s_ar` = Acm[b, p+i, rr[m]] = element (row rr[m], col p+i) = V_raw[rr[m], i]. Then `vchunk[i,m] = where(rr[m]==p+i, 1, where(rr[m]>p+i, vraw, 0))`. ✓ That gives vchunk[i,m] = V[rr[m], i]. ✓

3. **W = V^T C**: `tl.dot(vchunk[BLK,BM], cchunk[BM,BNc])`. vchunk[i,m]=V[rr[m],i], cchunk[m,g]=C[rr[m], gcol[g]]. So `W[i,g] = sum_m V[rr[m],i] * C[rr[m],gcol] = sum_r V[r,i] C[r,g]`. ✓ Correct = (V^T C)[i,g].

4. **YT = T^T W**: I want `YT[i,g] = sum_l T[l,i] W[l,g]` (since (T^T W)[i,g] = sum_l (T^T)[i,l] W[l,g] = sum_l T[l,i] W[l,g]). I load `Tt[i,l] = T[l,i]` and do `tl.dot(Tt, W)` → `YT[i,g] = sum_l Tt[i,l] W[l,g] = sum_l T[l,i] W[l,g]`. ✓ Correct.

   But wait — is `Tt[i,l] = T[l,i]`? Tg stores `T[i,l]` at `Tg[b,l,i]` (col-major `Tg[i + l*NBMAX]` → viewing as `(B,nb,nb)` contiguous, `Tg[b, slow, fast]` where slow=l, fast=i, so `Tg[b,l,i] = T[i,l]`). # Trailing-update tile shapes for the Triton tf32x3 kernels (mirrors worker-2's
# tuned per-kernel micro-sweep on the dominant B=640 n=512 panel):
#   YT (W=V^T@C reduces over tall pheight, BLK output rows): small tile + 1 warp.
#   apply (delta=Vrow@YT, disjoint output tiles): TALL-NARROW BM=128, BNc=32, 4w
#   (K=BLK pins BNc==BLK so the MMA's K dim isn't starved by a wide BNc).
_TC_YT = (32, 32, 1)        # (BM, BNc, num_warps)
_TC_APPLY = (128, 32, 4)


def _qr_cuda_coop2_tc(a: torch.Tensor, nb: int = 0) -> output_t:
    # coop2 with a TENSOR-CORE (tf32x3) trailing update. The CUDA panel kernel
    # (exact FP32 Householder + compact-WY T, on-chip) and transposes are kept;
    # only the trailing block-reflector update -- 85% of GPU time and previously
    # an FP32-SIMT ~1 TFLOP/s GEMM -- is replaced with two Triton tf32x3 tl.dot
    # kernels reading the column-major Acm in place. The Python loop alternates
    # CUDA panel -> Triton trailing; each kernel launch is the cross-CTA barrier.
    B, n, _ = a.shape
    if nb <= 0:
        nb = _coop_nb(n)
    H = torch.empty_like(a)
    Acm = torch.empty((B, n, n), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    Tg = torch.empty((B, nb, nb), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    tau = torch.empty((B, n), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    YT = torch.empty((B, nb, n), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    mod = _get_cuda_mod()

    s_ab, s_ac, s_ar = Acm.stride(0), Acm.stride(1), Acm.stride(2)
    s_tb, s_tl, s_ti = Tg.stride(0), Tg.stride(1), Tg.stride(2)
    s_yb, s_yk, s_yc = YT.stride(0), YT.stride(1), YT.stride(2)
    BM_Y, BNc_Y, NW_Y = _TC_YT
    BM_A, BNc_A, NW_A = _TC_APPLY

    mod.qr_coop2_transpose_in(a.data_ptr(), Acm.data_ptr(), B, n)
    p = 0
    while p < n:
        cur_nb = nb if p + nb <= n else n - p
        mod.qr_coop2_panel(Acm.data_ptr(), Tg.data_ptr(), tau.data_ptr(),
                           B, n, nb, p, cur_nb)
        jb = p + cur_nb
        ncols = n - jb
        if ncols > 0:
            nct_y = triton.cdiv(ncols, BNc_Y)
            _coop_trailing_YT_cm[(nct_y, B)](
                Acm, Tg, YT,
                B, n, p, cur_nb, ncols, jb,
                s_ab, s_ac, s_ar, s_tb, s_tl, s_ti, s_yb, s_yk, s_yc,
                BLK=nb, BM=BM_Y, BNc=BNc_Y, num_warps=NW_Y,
            )
            nct_a = triton.cdiv(ncols, BNc_A)
            nrt_a = triton.cdiv(n - p, BM_A)
            _coop_trailing_apply_cm[(nrt_a * nct_a, B)](
                Acm, YT,
                B, n, p, cur_nb, ncols, jb,
                s_ab, s_ac, s_ar, s_yb, s_yk, s_yc,
                BLK=nb, BM=BM_A, BNc=BNc_A, num_warps=NW_A,
            )
        p += cur_nb
    mod.qr_coop2_transpose_out(Acm.data_ptr(), H.data_ptr(), B, n)
    return H, tau

So locally, both CUDA `<<<>>>` (legacy default stream) and Triton (current stream = default stream) are on the same stream → no race locally. But my test showed a race **even locally**!

First win logged (6928us, 2.41x). Now the biggest lever is **n=4096 (228,781us)** — it dominates the geomean as the largest single value. The brief specifically calls this out: "n=4096, the ONE shape nothing in the run currently beats" geqrf's ~54k.

def _qr_cuda_coop2_tc_rm(a: torch.Tensor, nb: int = 16) -> output_t:
    # TRANSPOSE-FREE tf32x3 coop2: the CUDA panel factor and the Triton trailing
    # both operate on row-major A IN PLACE, so the two layout-shuffling transpose
    # kernels (qr_transpose_in/out, ~18% of n=512 GPU time) are eliminated. The
    # output H IS the factored A (geqrf packing). Triton kernels are layout-
    # agnostic: we pass A's row-major strides (column stride 1, row stride n).
    B, n, _ = a.shape
    H = a.clone()                       # factor in place; H is the row-major output
    Tg = torch.empty((B, nb, nb), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    tau = torch.empty((B, n), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    YT = torch.empty((B, nb, n), device=a.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    mod = _get_cuda_mod()

    # H is row-major (B,n,n): element(row r,col c) at H[b,r,c].  For the Triton
    # kernels' (s_ac=col stride, s_ar=row stride): col stride = 1, row stride = n.
    s_ab = H.stride(0)
    s_ac = H.stride(2)                  # move one column == last dim == 1
    s_ar = H.stride(1)                  # move one row == n
    s_tb, s_tl, s_ti = Tg.stride(0), Tg.stride(1), Tg.stride(2)
    s_yb, s_yk, s_yc = YT.stride(0), YT.stride(1), YT.stride(2)
    BM_Y, BNc_Y, NW_Y = _TC_YT
    BM_A, BNc_A, NW_A = _TC_APPLY

    p = 0
    while p < n:
        cur_nb = nb if p + nb <= n else n - p
        mod.qr_coop2_panel_rm(H.data_ptr(), Tg.data_ptr(), tau.data_ptr(),
                              B, n, nb, p, cur_nb)
        jb = p + cur_nb
        ncols = n - jb
        if ncols > 0:
            nct_y = triton.cdiv(ncols, BNc_Y)
            _coop_trailing_YT_cm[(nct_y, B)](
                H, Tg, YT,
                B, n, p, cur_nb, ncols, jb,
                s_ab, s_ac, s_ar, s_tb, s_tl, s_ti, s_yb, s_yk, s_yc,
                BLK=nb, BM=BM_Y, BNc=BNc_Y, num_warps=NW_Y,
            )
            nct_a = triton.cdiv(ncols, BNc_A)
            nrt_a = triton.cdiv(n - p, BM_A)
            _coop_trailing_apply_cm[(nrt_a * nct_a, B)](
                H, YT,
                B, n, p, cur_nb, ncols, jb,
                s_ab, s_ac, s_ar, s_yb, s_yk, s_yc,
                BLK=nb, BM=BM_A, BNc=BNc_A, num_warps=NW_A,
            )
        p += cur_nb
    return H, tau

**Key idea**: The panel kernel runs `B` blocks (one per matrix), each factoring a serial nb=16 column panel. The panel reads the sub-panel `(n-p)×nb` into smem then does 16 serial Householder steps. 

A structural improvement: **make nb larger** to reduce the number of panels (fewer trailing launches, fewer barriers), but the panel cost grows. OR **reduce the trailing kernel re-reads**. Let me take a different high-leverage angle: the **trailing apply + YT together are 45%**. These are tensor-core GEMMs. The YT computes W=V^T C (contraction over n rows). The apply computes delta = V @ YT. For n=512 b=640, the V matrix is 512×16 (rank 16), C is 512×496. The apply delta=V@YT is 512×496 = a rank-16 update. With BM=128, BNc=32, the apply does 4 row-tiles × 16 col-tiles = 64 programs/matrix × 640 = 40960 programs, each a 128×32 = small tile with K=16. **K=16 is tiny for tensor cores** (the MMA wants K>=16 but more is better).

content.text:
Wait — the kernel shows `Stream 7` for the panel kernel! `Stream 7` is NOT the default stream — confirming the CUDA `<<<>>>` launch and Triton are now BOTH on stream 7 (the row-major path uses Triton's current stream for everything... no wait, the CUDA panel uses `<<<>>>` which should be legacy default). Actually "Stream 7" is just how ncu labels the stream PyTorch uses (the current stream context). They appear to be on the same stream now (no race in RM path since validation passed). Good — but interesting that ncu calls it stream 7 (likely the per-process default).

Key findings:
- **`qr_panel_kernel`: ~191us/launch, 32 regs, occupancy_limit_shared_mem=9 blocks, sm__throughput=40%, compute_mem_throughput=57%.** The panel is NOT compute or memory bound (40% SM, 57% mem) — it's **latency-bound** (serial dependency chain + low occupancy). Only 32 registers but smem limits to 9 blocks/SM. The 40% SM throughput with 256 threads means warps are stalling on the serial Householder chain.
- **`_coop_trailing_apply_cm`: ~143us, 98 regs, sm__throughput=36%, mem=55%.** Also underutilized — 36% SM. K=16 MMA + the V/C re-reads. Not great.
- **`_coop_trailing_YT_cm`: ~63us, 147 regs(!), sm=57%.** Better utilized.

The apply kernel at 36% SM throughput with rank-16 is the issue — the MMA K=16 is small and the kernel re-reads V twice (once for YT, once for apply) + C. 

Biggest opportunities:
1. **Panel latency (191us×32 launches... no, per the full-run profile panel total was 62ms)**: occupancy limited to 9 blocks/SM by smem. At p=0, smem = 512×16×4 = 32KB → 227KB/32KB ≈ 7 blocks; ncu says 9 (smem decreases as p grows). With 640 matrices / (9 blocks × 148 SMs) the panel is latency-bound on the serial chain.

2. **The apply re-reads.** Worker-2 fuses better. 

Let me focus on a structural win for the apply kernel. Currently apply re-reads V in RB strips AND re-reads V again from the YT kernel. But the deeper issue: with K=16, tensor cores are underused. 

Actually — let me reconsider. The panel is 37%, apply 29.7%, YT 15.2%. **The apply kernel computes delta = V @ YT where V is 512×16, YT is 16×496, output 512×496.** This is a rank-16 outer-product-like GEMM. With K=16 the MMA does one 16×16×16 tile worth per step. Fine. The apply re-reads V (512×16) for each row strip and C... actually apply reads V once per output tile. 

Let me try a concrete tile sweep on the apply kernel since it's 30% and underutilized. Worker-2 used BM=128, BNc=32. Let me sweep BM in {64,128,256} and BNc in {16,32,64} and num_warps in {2,4,8}. Let me make the tiles env-configurable and sweep.

Actually, simpler and more impactful: let me reconsider whether I even need the **two-kernel split** (YT then apply). Worker-2 splits to avoid races. But I could **fuse** if I stage YT in smem... no, the race is real across row-tiles. 

Let me instead try the most promising structural change: **increase apply occupancy by using fewer registers / smaller tiles** OR **larger BM to amortize YT loads**. Let me sweep. Let me make `_TC_APPLY` and `_TC_YT` overridable by env for the sweep.

def run_rm(a, nb, ty, ta):
    B,n,_=a.shape
    H=a.clone(); Tg=torch.empty((B,nb,nb),device="cuda"); tau=torch.empty((B,n),device="cuda")
    YT=torch.empty((B,nb,n),device="cuda")
    mod=S._get_cuda_mod()
    s_ab=H.stride(0); s_ac=H.stride(2); s_ar=H.stride(1)
    s_tb,s_tl,s_ti=Tg.stride(); s_yb,s_yk,s_yc=YT.stride()
    BM_Y,BNc_Y,NW_Y=ty; BM_A,BNc_A,NW_A=ta
    p=0
    while p<n:
        cur_nb=nb if p+nb<=n else n-p
        mod.qr_coop2_panel_rm(H.data_ptr(),Tg.data_ptr(),tau.data_ptr(),B,n,nb,p,cur_nb)
        jb=p+cur_nb; ncols=n-jb
        if ncols>0:
            nct_y=triton.cdiv(ncols,BNc_Y)
            S._coop_trailing_YT_cm[(nct_y,B)](H,Tg,YT,B,n,p,cur_nb,ncols,jb,
                s_ab,s_ac,s_ar,s_tb,s_tl,s_ti,s_yb,s_yk,s_yc,BLK=nb,BM=BM_Y,BNc=BNc_Y,num_warps=NW_Y)
            nct_a=triton.cdiv(ncols,BNc_A); nrt_a=triton.cdiv(n-p,BM_A)
            S._coop_trailing_apply_cm[(nrt_a*nct_a,B)](H,YT,B,n,p,cur_nb,ncols,jb,
                s_ab,s_ac,s_ar,s_yb,s_yk,s_yc,BLK=nb,BM=BM_A,BNc=BNc_A,num_warps=NW_A)
        p+=cur_nb
    return H,tau

def bench(a,nb,ty,ta,iters=15):
    f=lambda: run_rm(a,nb,ty,ta)
    H,tau=f(); Q=torch.linalg.householder_product(H,tau);R=torch.triu(H)
    rel=(R-Q.transpose(-2,-1)@a).abs().max().item()/a.abs().max().item()
    if rel>1e-3: return None,rel
    for _ in range(3): f()
    torch.cuda.synchronize(); t0=time.perf_counter()
    for _ in range(iters): f()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return (time.perf_counter()-t0)/iters*1e6, rel

The **panel kernel (37%, latency-bound, 40% SM throughput)** is the wall. Let me think structurally. The panel factors one matrix per block, serially over nb=16 columns. The latency is the serial Householder chain. Key levers:

1. **Increase occupancy**: panel uses 32 regs, smem-limited to ~9 blocks/SM. At p=0 smem=(n-p)*16*4. For n=512 that's 32KB → 7 blocks/SM. As p grows, smem shrinks → more blocks. Can't easily reduce smem (need the sub-panel).

2. **Process the panel norm/update with more parallelism**: already uses 256 threads with warp-shuffle reductions.

3. **The real structural fix**: the panel does a **norm reduction (block sync) for every column** (16 syncs) + a batched trailing-panel-update. Each column k: compute norm (block reduce), compute beta/tau (thread 0), normalize, update trailing panel columns. The block reductions serialize. 

Let me look at whether reducing the number of `__syncthreads()` in the panel helps, or whether a fundamentally different panel (e.g., **Cholesky-of-Gram + triangular solve**, the "CholeskyQR" approach) would be much faster. 

**CholeskyQR2 idea**: For a panel (or the whole matrix), Q,R can be computed via: `G = A^T A` (tensor-core GEMM, fast), `R = chol(G)`, `Q = A R^-1` (triangular solve). Critical finding: **"55.85% of all local loads and 60.96% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 39.24% of [memory traffic]"** and **"Est. Speedup: 47-52%"** from fixing local memory. The panel kernel is spilling heavily to local memory.

The culprit: `float pw[NBMAX]` (16 floats) and `float pz[NBMAX]` register arrays. With only 32 registers/thread allocated, these 16-element arrays spill to local memory. The fix: **either reduce register pressure or increase the register budget.**

NBMAX=16 → `pw[16]`/`pz[16]` are large. But the code only uses `ntrail` (≤15) entries. Still, the compiler allocates the full array. Options:
1. **Increase registers per thread** via `__launch_bounds__` or compiler flag, so the arrays stay in registers (8 blocks limited by 32 regs → if I allow more regs, fewer blocks but no spilling). But spilling is worse than lower occupancy here (47% speedup estimate).
2. **Restructure to avoid the big register array.** The `pw[t]` accumulates partial dot products for each trailing column t in the batched panel update. This is inherently nb-wide.

Let me try the simplest high-impact fix: **add `__launch_bounds__(256, N)` to control occupancy and let the compiler use more registers** to avoid spilling. The panel kernel currently gets 32 regs (compiler-chosen for 8 blocks). If I set `__launch_bounds__(256, 4)` (target 4 blocks/SM), the compiler can use up to ~64 regs, eliminating the `pw`/`pz` spills.

@triton.jit
def _coop_trailing_fused_cm(
    Acm_ptr, Tg_ptr,
    B, n, p, nb, ncols, jb,
    s_ab, s_ac, s_ar,
    s_tb, s_tl, s_ti,
    BLK: tl.constexpr, BM: tl.constexpr, BNc: tl.constexpr,
):
    # ONE program owns a BNc-wide column tile and ALL its rows -- the block
    # reflector update C[:,g] -= V (T^T (V^T C[:,g])) is independent per column,
    # so there is NO cross-program race and YT need not round-trip through global
    # (saves the YTbuf write+read and a whole kernel launch vs the 2-kernel path).
    #   pass 1: W = V^T C   (reduce over all rows in BM strips)
    #   YT = T^T W
    #   pass 2: C -= V YT    (over all rows in BM strips)
    col_tile = tl.program_id(0)
    bid = tl.program_id(1)
    if bid >= B:
        return
    c0 = col_tile * BNc
    gcols = jb + c0 + tl.arange(0, BNc)
    gvalid = (c0 + tl.arange(0, BNc)) < ncols
    krange = tl.arange(0, BLK)
    kvalid = krange < nb
    base = Acm_ptr + bid * s_ab
    vcols = p + krange
    pheight = n - p
    nchunks = tl.cdiv(pheight, BM)

    # pass 1: W = V^T C
    W = tl.zeros((BLK, BNc), dtype=tl.float32)
    for ci in range(0, nchunks):
        rr = p + ci * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
        rmask = rr < n
        cp = base + gcols[None, :] * s_ac + rr[:, None] * s_ar
        cchunk = tl.load(cp, mask=rmask[:, None] & gvalid[None, :], other=0.0)  # (BM,BNc)
        vp = base + vcols[:, None] * s_ac + rr[None, :] * s_ar
        vraw = tl.load(vp, mask=kvalid[:, None] & rmask[None, :], other=0.0)
        rrm = rr[None, :]; diagr = vcols[:, None]
